title: acre render writes an animation as an MP4 file
body:
`acre render FILE --out PATH` writes a PNG, SVG or PDF of one instant. A drawing with a `canvas` `duration` is an animation, and `Canvas::frame_count` and `Canvas::time_of` in the `acre` library count its frames. Nothing writes the whole animation out.

## Proposal

`--out x.mp4`, or `--format mp4`, writes H.264 video.

- One frame every `1/fps` seconds from 0 through `duration` inclusive. `--fps N` overrides the canvas fps, 30 by default.
- `--scale` applies as for images and defaults to 1. An odd width or height is padded by one pixel of the background colour, since yuv420p needs even sizes.
- `acre-cli` starts `ffmpeg` found on `PATH` and writes raw RGB frames to its stdin.
- `--jobs N` draws frames on N threads, 1 by default, and feeds them to `ffmpeg` in frame order with at most two drawn frames waiting per thread.
- A drawing with no duration, or a `PATH` with no `ffmpeg`, is an error before anything is drawn. A failed export removes the partial file and prints ffmpeg's stderr.

## Out of scope

Piping to an outside program is a stopgap. The choice of an in-process encoder is on acre-d44121.
close_reason: Landed in 3f37925: render --out x.mp4 pipes frames to ffmpeg, with --fps and --jobs.
